probe.tool: clang-tidy clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores (Ubuntu LLVM 21.1.8) on a scratch copy of mbedtls 068ff080 with each row's initializer rewritten to an opaque call, so clang's own constant-initializer exemption cannot hide the answer; three configurations (default; +USE_PSA_CRYPTO/ECJPAKE/DTLS_SRTP/ECDHE_PSK; -KEEP_PEER_CERTIFICATE/-TLS1_3) so every row's declaration is preprocessor-live in the one that judged it
probe.question: can the initial value reach a read on some path (no intervening write)?

notes:
benchmarking_db 1214: delta-adjudication of the five aurora_lint 1171 rule changes (ARR01-C 1203 / ee053615, EXP43-C 1204 / 541a194e, MSC13-C 1205 / 3cf9bb06, MSC37-C+MSC07-C 1206 / b172ce98, API00-C+EXP34-C 1207 / 727be89b, all merged 2026-09-15) on mbedtls at 068ff080. Basis: real-world run 268 (sqc-0.5.0-e405089a, 2026-09-19, all 12 codebases); no commit after e405089a touches a rule. Pre-fix basis: run 256, the last run before the fixes landed (the run-257 build is the first with all five). REWORKED on Brandon's decision of 2026-09-20 (via the coordinator): a silenced MSC13-C row is flipped only if its initial value can reach a read, not because a merged exemption covers its shape.

MEASUREMENT FIRST. At run 268 every mbedtls finding of all seven rules is already labeled -- API00-C 883/883, EXP34-C 299/299, MSC13-C 355/355, MSC37-C 3/3, and ARR01-C / EXP43-C / MSC07-C fire 0 times -- so there is NO new-key population to adjudicate: the five fixes moved nothing onto an unlabeled line. Counting basis: distinct (file, line, rule) keys via BenchDB.list_realworld_unlabeled and get_realworld_findings, scope library/** (the scan path, so nothing to drop). The pull was also diffed against this repo's main CSV: identical key set for these rules.

WHAT MOVED, per rule, run 256 -> 268, by the label each silenced key carried: API00-C 1074 -> 883 (191 silent: 182 FP, 9 TP); ARR01-C 186 -> 0 (186 FP); EXP34-C 309 -> 299 (10 FP, 1 FN); EXP43-C 268 -> 0 (267 FP, 1 TP); MSC07-C 50 -> 0 (50 FP; its 1 FN never fired); MSC13-C 1065 -> 355 (710 silent: 618 FP, 92 TP); MSC37-C 185 -> 3 (182 FP). All 102 TP-labeled keys went silent at run 257 and at no other run since (checked per key against runs 255-268).

THE 102 SILENT TPs, EVERY ONE READ AT SOURCE. Two different things are among them, and this batch treats them differently:

(1) FLIPPED TP -> FP, 11 rows, because the finding was a misfire on the facts (ADR-0005) -- the construct the finding names is not there:
- API00-C, 9 rows (all library/ecp.c): include/mbedtls/ecp.h states the precondition on the flagged parameter in so many words ("This must not be NULL", "This must be initialized", "This must be initialized and have group parameters set"). aurora_lint 1207's stated policy: an explicit published precondition is validation placed on the caller by design; the oracle's other 1,034 mbedtls API00-C FP rows already read the convention that way (310 of their reasons say "precondition", 308 "contract", 424 "convention"), and these 9 carried one boilerplate reason. The 11 ecp.c API00-C TP rows that STILL fire (lines 248, 488, 504, 514, 536, 678, 846, 879, 913, 929) have no explicit wording in their \param text -- consistent, untouched.
- EXP43-C, 1 row (library/rsa_alt_helpers.c:217): mbedtls_mpi_div_mpi(&K, NULL, &K, D) passes one object as Q and A, against the header's "must not alias" note -- but no parameter of mbedtls_mpi_div_mpi is restrict-qualified, and EXP43-C governs restrict-qualified pointers only. The label described a documented-contract violation, which is not this rule. Whether it is a defect at all is outside this batch.
- MSC13-C, 1 row (library/pkwrite.c:312): 'ret' is written, tested and returned inside MBEDTLS_ASN1_CHK_ADD, invoked seven times in the function; the "declared but never used" finding and the label's "never referenced anywhere" both missed the header macro.

(2) KEPT TP, 91 rows: every MSC13-C declaration-initializer row the 1205 exemption silenced (80 named-constant initializers -- 54 x MBEDTLS_ERR_ERROR_CORRUPTION_DETECTED, 13 x PSA_ERROR_CORRUPTION_DETECTED, 3 x MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE, 2 x PSA_ERROR_GENERIC_ERROR, one each of MBEDTLS_ERR_MPI_NOT_ACCEPTABLE, MBEDTLS_ERR_ECP_BAD_INPUT_DATA, MBEDTLS_ERR_ASN1_INVALID_DATA, MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_NONE, PSA_SUCCESS, MBEDTLS_TLS_SRTP_UNSET, MBEDTLS_CT_FALSE, MBEDTLS_CT_TRUE -- and 11 literal initializers `int ret = 0` / `-1` on the returned variable). Each was put to one tool-provable test: CAN THE INITIAL VALUE REACH A READ ON SOME PATH, i.e. is there a path from the declaration to a use of the variable with no intervening write?

  THE PROBE (data/precision_audit/task1214/probe_deadstores.py, local working data). clang-tidy clang-analyzer-deadcode.DeadStores (Ubuntu LLVM 21.1.8) answers exactly that question over clang's own CFG with real preprocessing, so macro-hidden reads and writes (MBEDTLS_MPI_CHK, MBEDTLS_ASN1_CHK_ADD, PSA_TO_MBEDTLS_ERR) are seen. clang exempts a CONSTANT initializer that is later reassigned -- the same exemption as 1205 -- so on a scratch copy of the tree each row's initializer was rewritten to a call of an undefined extern function (opaque value) and the probe run per file; DeadStores then warns "Value stored to 'X' during its initialization is never read" iff no path reads the initial value. Controls, same tool and flags on a synthetic file: warns on plain overwrite, on a macro-only write (the pkwrite shape) and on a loop back-edge write; silent on an early `goto` that skips the assignment, on a branch that returns the initial value, and on a switch arm that falls to the return without writing. 17 of the 91 rows sit under options the default config leaves off (MBEDTLS_USE_PSA_CRYPTO, ECJPAKE, DTLS-SRTP, ECDHE-PSK, or !KEEP_PEER_CERTIFICATE); a declaration that the preprocessor's own line markers show as dead under one configuration was judged under the next (three configurations in all), never from a silent-because-unseen run. Every row's file compiled without error in the configuration that judged it.

  RESULT: 91 / 91 dead store. In every one, every path from the declaration overwrites the variable before any read of it -- the sentinel is defensive against a glitched control flow, not a value the C program can ever observe. reaches-use: 0. unclear: 0. Two rows were additionally hand-read as spot checks of the shapes most likely to be live (rsa.c:725 with five early literal returns; ssl_tls12_server.c:2466 with a switch whose every arm writes before `exit:`), agreeing with the tool. So under Brandon's test these are genuine dead stores and their TP labels stand. They are listed under exemption_1205_suppresses_a_true_dead_store in this manifest, which is the input to an aurora_lint task for narrowing 1205 from shape to dataflow; the manifest field `probe` records the method.

NOT TOUCHED: the 1,505 silent FP rows (the fixes agreeing with the oracle), the FN rows, every still-firing row, and the 91 rows above.

EFFECT ON THE LABELED SAMPLE (stated, not claimed as a project figure -- see aurora-lint CLAUDE.md): at run 268 API00-C is 31 TP / 883 (run 256: 40 / 1074), MSC13-C 46 / 355 (138 / 1065; after this batch the MSC13-C TP labels are 137, of which 91 are silenced by 1205 and read as FN at run 268 -- a recall effect of the exemption, which is the point of the list above), EXP34-C 3 / 299 (3 / 309), EXP43-C 0 / 0 (1 / 268), ARR01-C, MSC07-C, MSC37-C 0 TP of 0 / 0 / 3 fired.

MECHANICS, following task-1281 / task-1352: each corrected row carries this batch's source, adjudicator claude-opus-5, a reason quoting the one it supersedes, and this batch's adjudicated_at; the donor manifest (mbedtls-oracle-build-r720-20260914) gets row_count 8361 -> 8350 and a superseded_rows record naming the 11 keys. Reasons are label basis only.
